# Best open-ear earbuds for running

I can't open retailer pages from here. Most of the buy links below go to the review pages, which list the retailer buttons. Prices are as quoted in those reviews and may have changed.

## Top picks

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (about $199, down from $299)**
- Runner's World's top pick for sound quality and comfort. It says they don't bounce and play well with hats and glasses.
- WIRED likes the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run than touch controls.
- Downsides: IPX4 water resistance and about 7 hours per charge. Runner's World also says Bose has new open-ear earbuds coming soon, so consider waiting.
- [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) | [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 ($180 list, listed around $125 at Best Buy and REI)**
- Both Runner's World and WIRED recommend it for running. It has physical buttons, 12 hours of battery, and IP55 sweat resistance.
- Downsides: the neckband can interfere with long hair and winter hats. WIRED found the clarity a bit lower than the older OpenRun and the Bose.
- [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

**Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2 ($200)**
- 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating. WIRED names it best overall and wore it in rain and submerged it.
- The clip-on design leaves the top of your ear free for glasses or hats.
- [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

## Budget picks

- **Soundcore AeroFit 2:** IP55, 10 hours per charge (42 with the case), with an ear hook. SoundGuys picks it as best budget and lists it at $79.99 on Amazon ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)). A deal site, Dealectric, lists it at $129.99 and claims code AFSC20 brings it to $104 ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2)). That page is an affiliate site and its price is higher than SoundGuys' Amazon price, so compare before using the code.
- **JLab Flex Open (about $40):** Runner's World's budget pick. Sound is less rich than pricier pairs, but it's a low-risk way to try clip-ons. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro ($50):** WIRED's cheap pick. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Nothing Ear (Open) (about $99 on Amazon):** SoundGuys' best overall open-ear pick, with strong bass and an IP54 rating. [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

## Quick advice

- **Max awareness, bass-friendly:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.
- **Best sound and comfort:** Bose Ultra Open, or wait for Bose's upcoming pair.
- **Rain and marathon-length battery:** Shokz OpenDots 2.
- **Testing the category cheaply:** JLab Flex Open or Soundpeats PearlClip Pro.

Open-ear designs let in traffic noise but don't guarantee safety, so keep the volume reasonable.

If you tell me your budget, whether you wear glasses or hats, and whether you use iPhone or Android, I can narrow it to one.
